items.title: PM’s address at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi

candidate_claims.text: Excellencies, delegates from around the world, leaders from business and industry, policymakers, and my friends.
Reflecting on his 30-year journey, he mentioned that I am his friend.
Friends, This year’s Bloomberg Economic Forum is focused on the new powers emerging around the world.
But in the 21st century, especially in this third decade, a major transformation is taking place.
India has more than one hundred languages, nearly eighty thousand registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels.
And not only that, in this age of social media, India has more than five hundred million YouTube users and more than five hundred million Instagram users.
Friends, Until about twelve or thirteen years ago, there was a time in India when access to mobile phones and the internet itself was a form of power.
After 2014, when a new government came to power in India and we were given the opportunity to serve, India placed great emphasis on making mobile data affordable.
In other words, connectivity in India has not merely connected people; it has connected opportunities as well.
Before 2014, India had only a few hundred startups.
Today, the country has more than 250,000 startups.
Nearly half of these startups come from small cities and towns.
More than forty-five percent of startups have at least one woman Director or Partner.
In other words, opportunities for innovation are reaching more people, new talent is emerging, and new solutions are being created.
Following this path, India has lifted 250 million people out of poverty over the past decade, a number greater than the population of many countries in the world.
Friends, You may also have heard about the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer.
By using technology, we have created a system through which government assistance reaches beneficiaries directly in their bank accounts.
This has reduced corruption, increased convenience for citizens, and established a direct pathway between the government and the people.
We supplied vaccines to more than one hundred countries.
Nandan, who is seated here, can later share much more information about how this was done.
India achieved this milestone in November 2021 itself, nine years ahead of schedule.
This was not merely about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a reflection of India’s evolving energy journey.
Friends, In 2014, India’s renewable energy capacity stood at about 75 gigawatts.
Today, it has reached approximately 300 gigawatts.
In other words, we have added nearly four times more capacity.

candidate_promises.text: In 2015, we set ourselves the target of achieving 40 percent of our installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.

items.title: PM’s address during the launch of development projects in Chennai

candidate_claims.text: We are inaugurating many completed projects and laying foundations for new ones.
In October 2001, I took oath as Chief Minister.
In 2014, metro services operated in only five cities of the country.
In 2014, India’s metro network was about 250 kilometres.
Today, this network has crossed 1,100 kilometres.
As a result of these efforts, today we are the world’s second-largest mobile manufacturer.
Since 2014, our electronics exports have increased elevenfold.
Our defence exports have increased fiftyfold.
Friends, Because of this growth in manufacturing, millions of direct and indirect jobs have been created for the youth of the country.
And when such infrastructure is built, it creates a large number of employment opportunities at different levels.
Employment opportunities are also created in factories connected with cement, steel, and equipment, as well as in smaller companies.
And when a project is completed, improved connectivity helps industries and services move forward.
That is why the rail and road projects being inaugurated and launched today are going to be extremely important for the progress of Tamil Nadu.
With an investment of about seventeen thousand crore rupees, the VOC Port at Thoothukudi is being developed as a world-class mega container and green energy hub.
Once this project is completed, even the world’s ultra-large container vessels will be able to dock here easily.
Because of increased speed, the turnaround time of ships at ports has been reduced by half.
Therefore, through the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana and several other schemes, projects worth thousands of crores of rupees have been approved for Tamil Nadu.
Assistance is also being provided for purchasing transport vehicles to keep fish fresh.
Last year, our seafood exports reached their highest levels ever, both in quantity and value terms.

candidate_promises.text: Some will make daily travel easier.
Together, they will create jobs for young people across Tamil Nadu.
This will create new employment opportunities here and will also greatly help in reducing the country’s imports.
